raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran the changed-file pre-commit hooks.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable repository and test AGENTS.md rules.
- [ ] I added the required labels. The contributor account cannot set upstream labels; requested: `cat-bugfix`, `area:sparse_attention`, `op:DSA`, `orig-external`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: SM90 DSA indexer forward.

## Summary

The load warp writes the shared W tile using all 32 lanes, but the Q TMA completion only orders the issuing lane. Consumers can read other lanes' W stores without a handoff. The FP8 path has the same problem for K scale stores and uses one elected lane to release an entire warp's scale reads before the stage is reused.

Add an unaligned named barrier for W publication with the load warp and the actual consumer warpgroups (160 BF16 or 288 FP8 threads). For FP8, count each scale-loading lane in the KV full mbarrier and have each consumer lane release the empty stage after its reads. The existing Q/K TMA and MMA schedule, output contract and supported dtypes remain unchanged.

## Validation

On GH200 SM90, cuDNN 9.27.0.42, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CuTeDSL 4.8.1/cu13 and Compute Sanitizer 2026.1.1:

- New regression: 10 passed, covering BF16, FP8 packed THD, FP8 H32/H64 with more than two KV tiles, racecheck and synccheck. The four racecheck cases fail on develop with shared-memory hazards while their underlying numerical tests pass.
- Existing indexer boundary selection: 14 passed, 9 architecture-dependent skips, 56 deselected.
- Cold-compiled BF16 and FP8 H32/H64 reference cases: 3 passed in each of CuTeDSL 4.8.0/cu12, 4.8.0/cu13 and 4.8.1/cu12; the CUDA 13 framework/backend and driver were retained. The compiler flavors report CUDA 12.9 and 13.4.
- CUDA Graph capture/replay matched eager output and LSE after changing the weights, for BF16 and FP8. One short ABBA measurement, including graph replay overhead, had BF16 medians 10.61/10.71 us before and 10.56/10.58 us after; FP8 8.21/8.18 us before and 8.21/8.21 us after. This does not establish general performance.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

This is separate from #2252 and #2253, which address the sparse and dense score recomputation kernels rather than indexer forward.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Check warp-role shared-memory publication in the SM90 indexer forward."""
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+@pytest.mark.gpu_exclusive
+@pytest.mark.xdist_group(name="gpu_exclusive")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool", ["racecheck", "synccheck"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "case",
+    [
+        pytest.param("test_DSA_indexer_forward_wrapper_qh16_causal_block_boundary", id="bf16"),
+        pytest.param("test_DSA_indexer_forward_wrapper_fp8_sm90_thd_matches_dequant_reference", id="fp8-thd"),
+        pytest.param("test_indexer_forward_sm90_fp8_k_scale_reuse[32]", id="fp8-reuse-h32"),
+        pytest.param("test_indexer_forward_sm90_fp8_k_scale_reuse[64]", id="fp8-reuse-h64"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_indexer_forward_sm90_sanitizer(case, tool):
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (9, 0):
+        pytest.skip("requires SM90")
+    toolkit_sanitizer = Path(os.environ.get("CUDA_HOME", "/usr/local/cuda")) / "bin" / "compute-sanitizer"
+    sanitizer = str(toolkit_sanitizer) if toolkit_sanitizer.is_file() and os.access(toolkit_sanitizer, os.X_OK) else shutil.which("compute-sanitizer")
+    if sanitizer is None:
+        sanitizer = next((str(p) for p in sorted(Path("/usr/local").glob("cuda*/bin/compute-sanitizer"))), None)
+    if sanitizer is None:
+        pytest.skip("compute-sanitizer is not installed")
+    test_timeout = float(os.environ.get("CUDNN_TEST_TIMEOUT", "1500"))
+    timeout = min(300.0, 0.6 * test_timeout) if test_timeout > 0 else 300.0
+    child = f"import faulthandler,sys; faulthandler.dump_traceback_later({timeout * 0.9!r}); import pytest; sys.exit(pytest.main(sys.argv[1:]))"
+    target = (
+        Path(__file__).resolve()
+        if case.startswith("test_indexer_forward_sm90_fp8_k_scale_reuse")
+        else Path(__file__).with_name("test_DSA_indexer_forward.py").resolve()
+    )
+    cmd = [
+        sanitizer,
+        "--tool",
+        tool,
+        "--report-api-errors",
+        "no",
+        "--error-exitcode",
+        "9",
+        "--print-limit",
+        "10",
+        sys.executable,
+        "-u",
+        "-c",
+        child,
+        f"{target}::{case}",
+        "-n0",
+        "-o",
+        "addopts=",
+        "-p",
+        "no:cacheprovider",
+        "-q",
+    ]
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, start_new_session=True)
+    try:
+        out, _ = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
+        os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        rest, _ = proc.communicate()
+        prior = exc.output.decode(errors="replace") if isinstance(exc.output, bytes) else (exc.output or "")
+        raise AssertionError(f"{tool} timed out after {timeout}s\n{prior}{rest}") from None
+    assert proc.returncode == 0, out[-8000:]
+    assert "1 passed" in out, out[-8000:]
+    summary = "ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors" if tool == "synccheck" else "0 errors, 0 warnings"
+    assert summary in out, out[-8000:]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+@pytest.mark.gpu_exclusive
+@pytest.mark.xdist_group(name="gpu_exclusive")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads", [32, 64])
+def test_indexer_forward_sm90_fp8_k_scale_reuse(heads):
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (9, 0):
+        pytest.skip("requires SM90")
+    from cudnn import DSA
+    from deepseek_sparse_attention.cutedsl.dsa_reference import ref_indexer_forward
+    from deepseek_sparse_attention.cutedsl.dsa_utils import quantize_fp8_1x128
+
+    torch.manual_seed(111 + heads)
+    batch, seq_q, seq_k, dim, ratio = 1, 8, 259, 128, 4
+    q_ref = torch.randn(batch, seq_q, heads, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    k_ref = torch.randn(batch, seq_k, 1, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    weights = torch.randn(batch, seq_q, heads, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.1
+    q, q_scale = quantize_fp8_1x128(q_ref)
+    k, k_scale = quantize_fp8_1x128(k_ref)
+    offsets = torch.tensor([seq_k * ratio - seq_q], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    result = DSA.indexer_forward_wrapper(
+        q,
+        k,
+        weights,
+        ratio=ratio,
+        qhead_per_kv_head=heads,
+        q_causal_offsets=offsets,
+        precision="fp8",
+        q_scale=q_scale,
+        k_scale=k_scale,
+        return_lse=True,
+    )
+    expected = ref_indexer_forward(
+        q.float() * q_scale.unsqueeze(-1),
+        k.float() * k_scale.unsqueeze(-1),
+        weights,
+        ratio,
+        q_causal_offsets=offsets,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(result["scores"], expected, atol=3e-3, rtol=3e-3)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(result["lse"], torch.logsumexp(expected, dim=-1), atol=5e-3, rtol=5e-3)
